boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten campus study settings ranging from quiet library space and reservable rooms to student lounges, academic commons, and an outdoor garden.

cards.title: Settle Into Bishop Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet and collaborative study space
cards.notes: Choose a quiet or collaborative area, then bring your LVC login if you expect to use a library computer or print coursework.
cards.short_summary: The main library supports both focused work and group sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC states that Bishop Library provides collaborative and quiet study spaces, study rooms, conference rooms, computers, printing, and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Summer 2026 hours are Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–4 p.m., Friday 8 a.m.–noon, and weekends closed; some spaces have limited availability during renovations.

cards.title: Book a Bishop Study Room
cards.subtitle: Tech-enabled rooms for contained group work
cards.notes: Request a study room through the library’s internal student site before a group session, and confirm renovation-related availability.
cards.short_summary: Reservable library rooms provide a defined setting for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The official library page says Bishop Library features tech-enabled study rooms and directs students, faculty, and staff to an internal site to request one.
cards.access_notes: Room requests are available to students, faculty, and staff through LVC’s internal library website; current renovations may limit availability.

cards.title: Plan a Session in Bishop-Frock
cards.subtitle: A named conference room inside Bishop Library
cards.notes: Use this for a planned meeting rather than an impromptu desk stop, and verify room access with the library before gathering.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated conference room offers a structured setting for scheduled academic collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC’s current campus map identifies the Bishop-Frock Conference Room inside the Vernon and Doris Bishop Library.
cards.access_notes: Conference-room access and reservation requirements are not stated on the public map; confirm availability with Bishop Library.

cards.title: Read by the Wengert Fireplace
cards.subtitle: Living-room seating in Mund College Center
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work that suits a shared student-center room, and check the day’s events before choosing a seat.
cards.short_summary: A fireplace and living-room format make this a distinct alternative to library seating.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC’s virtual tour specifically recommends studying in the Wengert Living Room by the fireplace, and the campus map lists its full name.
cards.access_notes: Located in Mund College Center; the public page does not state room hours, so use it while the building is unlocked and not hosting an event.

cards.title: Reset in the Commuter Lounge
cards.subtitle: Lower-level Mund study space for commuting students
cards.notes: Commuters can bring lunch, spread out between classes, and use the refrigerator, microwave, water cooler, or Keurig while studying.
cards.short_summary: This designated commuter hub combines study seating with practical between-class amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC says the Commuter Lounge is a central hub for commuting students to study, dine, and relax, with a microwave, refrigerator, water cooler, and Keurig.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Lebegern Learning Commons on Mund College Center’s lower level and intended for commuting students; public hours are not listed.

cards.title: Work Near Academic Support
cards.subtitle: A renovated lower-level commons in Mund
cards.notes: Use the commons when a task may benefit from nearby academic-success, accessibility, global-education, or career-development staff.
cards.short_summary: The learning commons places independent work near several student-support centers.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC describes the renovated Lebegern Learning Commons as a student success hub housing academic success, accessibility, global education, and career-development services.
cards.source_title: Welcome Week at the Lebegern Learning Commons
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of Mund College Center; individual support offices may require appointments or observe separate operating hours.

cards.title: Pause in Synodinos Commons
cards.subtitle: A named commons in Clyde A. Lynch Memorial Hall
cards.notes: Try this commons for laptop work between classes in Lynch, keeping the shared academic-building setting suitable for quiet conversation.
cards.short_summary: A named commons provides an identifiable shared workspace within an academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: The current official campus map places Synodinos Commons in Clyde A. Lynch ’18 Memorial Hall, and LVC depicts lounge desks in that building on its academic-resources page.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to Clyde A. Lynch Memorial Hall being unlocked and any activities scheduled in the commons; public hours are not posted.

cards.title: Bring Computer Work to Mund Tech
cards.subtitle: Technology space in Mund College Center
cards.notes: Choose this named technology area for computer-centered coursework, and confirm current equipment access or support availability on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused campus space offers an alternative setting for digital assignments.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC lists the Mund Technology Center on the lower level of Mund College Center and identifies it as a space desirable to commuting students.
cards.access_notes: Located on Mund College Center’s lower level; the public sources do not specify hours, equipment eligibility, or reservation rules.

cards.entity_name: Jeanne and Edward H. Arnold Health Professions Pavilion
cards.title: Study in the Health Professions Pavilion
cards.subtitle: An academic-building option for between-class work
cards.notes: Use the pavilion for coursework between health-sciences commitments, and avoid scheduled teaching or clinical areas unless authorized.
cards.short_summary: The health-professions building is documented as a useful campus stop for commuting students.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC’s commuter-resources page names the Jeanne and Edward H. Arnold Health Professions Pavilion among campus spaces especially useful to commuting students.
cards.access_notes: Use shared areas only while the academic building is unlocked; classrooms, laboratories, and clinical spaces may have restricted access.

cards.title: Take Reading to the Peace Garden
cards.subtitle: An outdoor campus setting for portable study
cards.notes: Bring reading, notes, or a charged device on a fair-weather day, and switch indoors when rain, heat, or low light makes work impractical.
cards.short_summary: This documented outdoor destination suits coursework that does not require a desk or power outlet.
cards.evidence_claim: LVC’s virtual tour identifies the Peace Garden as a campus outdoor space for relaxing in the fresh air and provides an official image of it.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor, weather-dependent space; the official page does not document lighting, electrical outlets, seating capacity, or overnight access.

warnings: Bishop Library reports limited space availability during its summer 2026 renovation; verify conditions before visiting.
Public sources do not provide current room-level coordinates or authoritative Google Maps URLs, so those fields are null.
The Peace Garden is documented as a relaxation space rather than a formally designated study area; its study use is limited to portable coursework.
